subject: Post-call: key custody + telemetry requirements for AceroHealth integration
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@acerohealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: key custody + telemetry requirements for AceroHealth integration

Hi Priya / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned from Redwood’s side:

Summary of requirements we heard:
- PII scoped to PHI-level data: retention policy is minimum 7 years for audit/clinical reasons, but must support shorter retention per dataset on request.
- Strong preference for customer key control for at-rest encryption. Current Acero environment uses Azure Key Vault (HSM-backed keys).
- Audit logging: full request/response telemetry (redacted content) and an immutable audit stream retained for 1 year; longer retention (>=7y) via export acceptable.
- Transport: mutual TLS required between Acero services and private deployment endpoints; hosted API must support mTLS or a private VPC connection.

Options we highlighted on the call (high level):
1) Hosted w/Redwood-managed keys — fastest to ship, Redwood holds keys, full signing/audit available, but not first-choice per your security team.
2) Hosted w/customer-managed KMS integration — Redwood integrates with customer Azure Key Vault (BYOK) using short-lived credentials + envelope encryption; Redwood never persists raw key material.
3) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — customer-owned HSM or Azure-managed HSM in their VPC; Redwood runtime connects to that KMS; full network isolation and key custody.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Priya: please confirm the Azure Key Vault SKU you use (Standard vs. Premium/HSM) and whether you require attestation/evidence of HSM backing.
- Tom (procurement): any non-standard contract terms around key custody or audit log retention we should be aware of?
- Jordan / Lauren / Aditya (internal): I’ve looped you in to draft an integration approach and a short artifact we can share with Acero (see attached one-pager).

Attachments: redwood-security-summary.pdf (one-page summary of the three options and evidence links).

I’ll follow up with a deeper technical note from Jordan with concrete integration steps and a proposed timeline. Would you prefer a technical workshop next week or a written design?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni

Subject: Re: Post-call: key custody + telemetry requirements for AceroHealth integration

Vivek — thanks for the concise recap. A couple clarifications from our security/compliance side: 

1) Key material / KMS: we are on Azure Key Vault Premium (HSM-backed). We will need written confirmation that the integration supports HSM-backed keys and that Redwood does not export raw key material.

2) mTLS: For hosted endpoints we will accept private connectivity via a VPC peering / PrivateLink-like approach to avoid public exposure; if hosted mTLS is offered as an alternative, we need mutual cert rotation and PKI requirements documented.

3) Audit logs / telemetry: we cannot permit raw PHI to be stored in Redwood logs. Redacted telemetry (hashes or prefixes) is acceptable. We also require an immutable audit stream with signed entries; retention for 1y on Redwood side and quarterly export to our archive for 7y retention.

4) Compliance evidence: please attach SOC 2 Type II summary and an architectural diagram showing where key custody lives in each option.

I attached our internal crypto/infra matrix (acero-crypto-requirements.xlsx) which lists a few non-negotiables.

If you can provide the HSM evidence and a short design doc, we’ll route to our Infosec for quick review. Workshop would be helpful — propose Wed 7/7 for a 60-minute deep dive (we are on PST).

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Head of Security Engineering, AceroHealth
priya@acerohealth.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: key custody + telemetry requirements for AceroHealth integration

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear asks. Below are concrete responses and a proposed minimal design that meets Acero’s constraints.

A. HSM-backed keys / BYOK:
- We support Azure Key Vault Premium (HSM) integration. Redwood never persistently stores raw key material; we use envelope encryption where your KMS performs the key unwrap operation. 
- Integration modes:
  * Hosted + BYOK (recommended for speed): Redwood calls your Azure Key Vault via a short-lived service principal that can delegate unwrap-only permissions. KMS calls happen in your region; we never export private keys.
  * Private (VPC) + customer HSM: for maximum isolation we deploy the runtime into your VPC and configure the runtime to call your HSM/Key Vault over private network. This also satisfies requirement for private connectivity and cert management.

B. Transport security (mTLS/private link):
- Hosted: we can offer PrivateLink endpoints per account + mTLS option. Cert rotation follows a mutually agreed schedule; Redwood supports automated rotation via ACME for Redwood-managed certs or manual rotation for customer-provided certs.
- Private: all traffic stays in your VPC — mutual certs can be handled by your PKI.

C. Telemetry & Logging:
- We will implement redaction rules to strip PHI from logs; our default is to redact full-text fields and persist message digests (SHA-256 prefixes) for traceability.
- Immutable audit stream: Redwood can sign and stream audit entries to your archive via an append-only log export (S3 with object lock or Azure Blob immutable storage). We’ll provide a structured JSON line export schema and signing proof.

D. Evidence / Artifacts we can provide quickly:
- SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted report) and SOC audit contact.
- Architecture diagram for BYOK vs. Private deployment (link below).
- Integration playbook with required IAM permissions, sample terraform for Azure KV, and runtime config snippets.

Action items / timeline:
- By EOD Wed (6/30): Vivek to share SOC 2 summary (done — attached earlier) and our one-pager.
- By Mon (7/5): Jordan to prepare integration playbook + architecture diagram (internal doc link below).
- Proposed workshop: Wed 7/7 10:00–11:00 PT — Jordan + Lauren to lead technical deep dive; Vivek to attend for commercial/contract questions.

Links / attachments:
- Integration playbook (internal): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-kms-integration

If this matches your expectations I’ll prepare the playbook and an example request/response audit export for review.

—Jordan Blake
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
